- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model should adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior forecast, especially if recent price action shows downward momentum.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.50), model should not over-forecast; cap upward revisions at +0.5% above prior 18-day average to avoid overshoot.
- After a price spike (e.g., >72.5), model tends to overcorrect and forecast a prolonged upward trend; apply a “mean reversion” penalty: subtract 0.3–0.7% per day after peak for 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day for next 3–5 days to avoid lagged overreaction.
